export const meta = {
  name: 'wall-slope-diagnose-design',
  description: 'Diagnose the posterior wall slope error on aligned grids and score three candidate fixes on phantoms',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Diagnose', detail: 'three lenses on why body.posterior_wall_slope errs on grids aligned with the frame' },
    { title: 'Design', detail: 'three candidate wall-slope readers, each scored on the same 98 cached phantoms' },
    { title: 'Judge', detail: 'pick the reader to put into body.py' },
  ],
}

const S = '/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/cbdcd57f-bcf8-5a71-ab64-4f0b9fbdb74f/scratchpad'
const CTX = `
You are working on bordercall's morphometry engine (a private research repository; confidential, nothing goes public).
Checkout: /home/user/bordercall, branch claude/project-thread-e89pjg (bordercall PR 44). Python: ${S}/venv/bin/python (numpy, scipy, nibabel, matplotlib), always with PYTHONPATH=/home/user/bordercall and OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 (four CPUs are shared by several agents).

Hard rules:
- Do NOT edit any file under /home/user/bordercall, and do not commit, push, switch branches or touch GitHub. Write only under the scratch folder named in your task.
- Never run anything under bordercall's archive/ folder (read it at most).
- Phantoms only: no real mask or CT is read in this container. Never send or start a grid job.
- No new dependencies (numpy, scipy, nibabel are allowed). Write scripts as files and run them by path.
- Report numbers you measured, from runs you made; say plainly what you did not measure.

The problem. morphometry/body.py posterior_wall_slope(v, B, xc) returns dy/dz of the vertebral body's posterior wall in the vertebra's own frame (x right, y anterior toward the body, z cranial): it keeps the body points B within ACROSS_HALF_MM (3 mm) of the midline xc, bins them in z over the middle 60 percent of the height with step max(v.fz, 0.5) mm, takes the least y (the most posterior point) of each bin and fits a line. Three readings are taken against the plane square to that wall, so they inherit its error: pedicle.one_side's pedicle_angle_sagittal (raw climb minus atan(wall)), body.inclinations' endplate_incl and endplate_lower_incl (-(rim slope + atan(wall))), and posterior.spinous_angle (+atan(wall)). anatomy.py has a separate wall_slope(z, y) for the canal's wall line, used for the body's cut and canal_ap_lateral_film; it is not the subject here, but say if it shares the mechanism.

Measured so far (score.py on the cache, frame-relative truth): on 1 mm slices the current reader errs by up to 1.72 degrees (grid tilted 2 degrees about x), 0.96 at 5 degrees, 0.57 on a grid exactly aligned, about 0.1 at the test suite's 18-degree tilt; on 2.5 mm slices up to 4.93 (tilt 2), 2.14 (tilt 10), 1.49 (aligned). An earlier probe found 1.8 to 4.2 degrees on three phantoms at tilt 2, 1 mm slices. The frame itself is right to 0.07 degrees on thin slices, but on 2.5 mm slices at small tilts it errs by 1.6 to 2.6 degrees; score.py compares the wall against the truth taken into the measured frame, so frame error is not counted against the wall.

The phantoms. morphometry/tests/phantom.py draws each vertebra in its own frame with the body's posterior wall at y = 0 (vertical) and labels a voxel when its centre falls inside a part. ${S}/wall/build_cache.py builds 98 configs: phantoms straight (wall leans 0, +5, -5 degrees, drawn by shearing the body's inside test), pitched, shapes (lean 0 and +4), pitched_down; grids aligned (tilt 0), x2, x5, x10 (tilts about x), suite18 ((1,0.3,0) 18 degrees, turn 7), t25, y12; spacings thin (0.8, 0.8, 1.0) and thick (0.86, 0.86, 2.5). Each pickle in ${S}/wall/cache/ holds {cfg, vert (the anatomy Vertebra of L3), truth, raw, frame_err_deg, wall_truth_deg, xc}. ${S}/wall/score.py scores any candidate: \`cd ${S}/wall && PYTHONPATH=/home/user/bordercall ${S}/venv/bin/python score.py cache <candidate.py> <function> --json <out.json>\` (use "current x" in place of a file to score the reader as it stands). A candidate has the signature fn(v, B, xc) -> dy/dz, or (dy/dz, info dict), or NAN to refuse. Read score.py and build_cache.py first. The cache should hold 98 pickles; if fewer, the build is still running (four processes): work on what is there and score again at the end.

Useful code to read: morphometry/body.py (posterior_wall_slope, inclinations, plate_rims), morphometry/pedicle.py (lattice_under, parting and slope_range: a linear-program parting of bone from air centres on the scan's own lattice, with the range of slopes that still part it; one_side; wall_slope), morphometry/anatomy.py (the Vertebra: frame, grid, is_bone, points_world, fx fy fz, pixel, body_pts, loc, wall_slope), scanimport/geometry.py.
`

const DIAG = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    mechanism: { type: 'string', description: 'what makes the reading err, in plain sentences' },
    confirmed: { type: 'boolean' },
    evidence: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'each a measured fact with its numbers' },
    implications_for_fix: { type: 'string' },
    files_written: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['mechanism', 'confirmed', 'evidence', 'implications_for_fix'],
}

const CAND = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    name: { type: 'string' },
    file: { type: 'string', description: 'absolute path of the candidate module' },
    function: { type: 'string' },
    summary: { type: 'string', description: 'how it reads the wall, in plain sentences' },
    score_json: { type: 'string' },
    score_summary: { type: 'string', description: 'the == thin and == thick blocks score.py printed, verbatim' },
    thin_max_err: { type: 'number' }, thin_median_err: { type: 'number' },
    thick_max_err: { type: 'number' }, thick_median_err: { type: 'number' },
    refused: { type: 'integer', description: 'configs where it returned NAN' },
    seconds_per_config: { type: 'number' },
    risks: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'how it could fail on real masks' },
  },
  required: ['name', 'file', 'function', 'summary', 'score_summary', 'thin_max_err', 'thick_max_err', 'refused', 'risks'],
}

const JUDGE = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    winner: { type: 'string' },
    combine: { type: 'string', description: 'what to graft from the others, or none' },
    reasons: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    gate: { type: 'string', description: 'when the slope should be refused or flagged, with the bound and its calibration' },
    expected: { type: 'string', description: 'the errors to expect, thin and thick, by grid' },
    implementation_notes: { type: 'string', description: 'exactly what body.posterior_wall_slope should become, and what else must change' },
  },
  required: ['winner', 'reasons', 'expected', 'implementation_notes'],
}

phase('Diagnose')
const lenses = [
  { key: 'binning', prompt: `Lens: the binning. Test the hypothesis that posterior_wall_slope's z bins (step max(fz, 0.5), centred on a grid of the frame's z, with the least y per bin) alias against the scan's lattice when the grid lies within a few degrees of the frame: bins that catch no lattice layer at the wall, or two, so the least y jumps, and the jumps drift one way over the height and bias the fit. Print, for the cached straight phantom at x2 and x5 (thin and thick) and at suite18, each bin's z, count, least y and which lattice layers (the scan's own k index, from v.grid) its points come from. Then say whether the error is this aliasing, the binary staircase of the wall itself, or something else, with numbers. Scratch folder: ${S}/wall/diag_binning/.` },
  { key: 'limit', prompt: `Lens: the information limit. A binary mask on a lattice pins a near-vertical wall's slope only so far. For every cached config, compute the interval of slopes b of a line y = a + b z (and of a plane y = a + b z + c x) that parts the body's bone centres within 3 mm of the midline over the middle 60 percent of the height from the non-body centres just behind the wall (use the vertebra's own lattice: v.grid, v.is_bone or the body's label, as pedicle.lattice_under does; decide carefully what counts as not-body behind the wall, since the canal lies there), by linear programs (scipy.optimize.linprog, method highs). Report per grid and spacing the interval's width in degrees, whether the frame-relative truth lies inside it, and where the widest-margin line falls in it. This bounds what any reader can do. Scratch folder: ${S}/wall/diag_limit/.` },
  { key: 'consumers', prompt: `Lens: the consumers and the second wall. (1) List every reader of body.posterior_wall_slope and of pedicle.wall_slope, and every place in morphometry/ and morphoview/ that reads anatomy's v.wall_slope, with what each does with it, and which tests in morphometry/tests/test_morphometry.py and morphoview/tests/ cover each and at which grid tilt and turn (P.draw's default grid_turn, P.straight's default tilt). (2) Measure on the cache whether anatomy's v.wall_slope (the canal wall's line) errs by the same mechanism on aligned grids (compare it with the frame-relative truth of the posterior wall, which on these phantoms is also the canal's anterior wall at the midline). (3) research_notes/morphometry/README.md says "the slabs' canal walls lean half as far as the posterior wall does, a cause in scanimport not found"; say whether these numbers bear on that. (4) Name any test that would change if the wall reader changed. Read-only on the repository; scratch folder ${S}/wall/diag_consumers/.` },
]
const diag = await parallel(lenses.map(l => () =>
  agent(CTX + '\n\nYour task.\n' + l.prompt, { label: 'diagnose:' + l.key, phase: 'Diagnose', schema: DIAG })
    .then(r => r ? { key: l.key, ...r } : null)))
const diagOk = diag.filter(Boolean)
log(`diagnose: ${diagOk.length} of ${lenses.length} lenses returned`)
const DIAG_TEXT = JSON.stringify(diagOk, null, 1)

phase('Design')
const designs = [
  { key: 'lattice', prompt: `Candidate A, lattice-native. Read the wall on the scan's own lattice, not on bins of the frame's z: for each lattice layer (and row) that crosses the wall band near the midline, take the posterior-most body centre (or the midpoint between it and the first non-body centre behind it), in frame coordinates, and fit the line through all of them, so that no layer is missed or caught twice. Consider using the whole middle 60 percent and a band in x wider than 3 mm if the wall allows.` },
  { key: 'parting', prompt: `Candidate B, parted by a linear program. As pedicle.parting does for the pedicle's surfaces: part the body's bone centres near the wall from the not-body centres just behind it by the line or plane of widest margin (scipy.optimize.linprog, highs), the slope its b, with the range of slopes that still part them (as pedicle.slope_range) returned in info, a least-crossing program where no line parts them, and a refusal where the range is too wide or the crossing too far. Decide what counts as not-body behind the wall (the canal is there; the posterior elements are further back).` },
  { key: 'boundary', prompt: `Candidate C, boundary midpoints by least squares. Take every pair of lattice-neighbouring centres across the posterior wall (body inside, not-body outside, along the lattice direction nearest the frame's y) within the band and the middle 60 percent, put the wall point at the pair's midpoint, and fit y = a + b z (+ c x if it helps) by least squares, perhaps robustly (a few iterations of trimming), so that every phase of the staircase is averaged.` },
]
const cands = await parallel(designs.map(d => () =>
  agent(CTX + `\n\nWhat the diagnosis found (three lenses, JSON):\n${DIAG_TEXT}\n\nYour task. Write one candidate wall reader as a module ${S}/wall/cand_${d.key}/cand.py with a function slope(v, B, xc) returning (dy/dz, info) or (NAN, info) to refuse, score it with score.py on the full cache (all 98 pickles; if the build is not finished when you start, develop on what is there and score again at the end), and report. ${d.prompt} Keep it short and readable, plain names, no new dependencies, and time it. Do not tune to the cache's truths beyond setting a bound you can justify from the geometry, and say which bound you set and why. If the information-limit lens shows a config cannot be pinned, say whether your reader refuses it or reads it.`,
    { label: 'design:' + d.key, phase: 'Design', schema: CAND }).then(r => r ? { key: d.key, ...r } : null)))
const candOk = cands.filter(Boolean)
log(`design: ${candOk.length} of ${designs.length} candidates returned`)

phase('Judge')
const verdict = await agent(CTX + `\n\nWhat the diagnosis found:\n${DIAG_TEXT}\n\nThe candidates (JSON, each with its score file):\n${JSON.stringify(candOk, null, 1)}\n\nYour task. Judge which reader should replace body.posterior_wall_slope. Re-run score.py yourself on each candidate's file to check its numbers (do not trust the summaries), read each candidate's code for what would break on real masks (a body whose posterior wall is concave or carries an osteophyte, a basivertebral foramen, a body cut by the volume's edge, a mask with holes), and weigh accuracy on thin and thick slices, refusals, simplicity and cost. Say what to graft from the runners-up, whether and when to refuse or flag, and exactly what body.posterior_wall_slope should become. Scratch folder ${S}/wall/judge/.`,
  { label: 'judge', phase: 'Judge', schema: JUDGE })

return { diagnose: diagOk, candidates: candOk, verdict }

diagnose.mechanism:
The hypothesis is wrong as stated. The z bins do not miss or double-catch the wall in a way that drifts. At the current step max(fz, 0.5), no bin in the 98 configs (1,091 bins) is empty, and none has its least-y point inside the body away from the wall (0 "alias" bins). At x2 every bin's wall points come from exactly one lattice layer, consecutive k, none skipped.

Three things make the reading err, in order of size.

(1) The binary staircase of the wall on the lattice. In each layer the least y is the first voxel centre in front of the wall. Its excess over the true wall drifts by tan(rel) per mm, where rel is the angle between the wall and the nearest lattice plane: +0.035 mm per 1 mm layer at 2 degrees. It drops by one row pitch (about 0.77 mm) where the wall crosses a row. The period is pitch/tan(rel), 22.9 mm at 2 degrees on thin slices. The window is the middle 60 percent of a 27 mm body, 16.2 mm, so at small rel it holds one drop or none. The fitted line then follows the lattice or the drop, not the wall. This is the "binary staircase of the wall itself". The jumps the hypothesis saw are these row steps (j changes), not bin effects.

(2) The body cut. B is everything in front of anatomy.body_in_front's canal-wall line. That line comes from anatomy.wall_slope over the canal's full-ring slab edges, and it has the same staircase, worse, because it uses fewer slabs: 4 on thick slices, and the rings cover only part of the height. Where the line leans wrongly it sits in front of the true wall at the low end of the window. It removes the wall's first voxel row there, so those bins read the cut line, not the mask. Bone lies directly behind the least-y point in 2 of 16 bins (x2 thin), 2 of 7 (x2 thick) and 4 of 16 (pitched and shapes x2 thin). This adds a forward step of one voxel at the bottom and pushes the slope negative.

(3) A small true binning term. The fit uses each bin's centre z, not its least-y point's own z. On thick slices the step (for example 2.585) is a little larger than the layer pitch along frame z. So some bins hold two layers' wall points, the least y takes whichever is lower or upper according to the sign of the wall's slope, and the point's z jumps from -1.21 to +1.17 mm off the bin centre between neighbouring bins. That misplaces the abscissa and steepens a wall that slopes in the frame. It is at most 0.89 degrees on thick slices, where the wall slopes 6.85 degrees in the frame (lean 5 plus 1.85 degrees of frame error), and at most 0.17 on thin slices.

anatomy.wall_slope's canal line shares mechanism (1). Its slab anterior edges show the same sawtooth: +0.03 to +0.04 mm per mm with a 0.76 mm drop on x2 thin. It errs by -2.51 (x2 thin), -4.50 (x2 thick) and -7.72 degrees (shapes x2 thick, which also has one slab edge 24 mm in front of the wall). Through the cut, that error feeds into posterior_wall_slope.
evidence: Cache complete: 98 pickles. My replica of the bin loop matches body.posterior_wall_slope to 0.0 degrees on all 98.

Over 98 configs and 1,091 bins at the current step: 0 empty bins, 0 bins whose least-y point has bone behind it inside B but outside the bin (aliasing), 35 bins where bone lies behind the point but outside B (the body cut binds), 275 bins whose wall points come from two or more lattice layers (alias.txt).

straight lean0 x2 thin, per bin (bins_straight.txt): 16 bins of step 1.027 over 16.2 mm. Each bin's wall points come from one layer, k = 141 to 156 in order. The least y's excess over the true wall rises by +0.035 per bin within a row and drops by 0.765 at the j step 143 -> 142 (bin 3) and by 0.633 at 142 -> 141 (bin 15). The fit of the excess over bin z is -1.73 degrees against a reader error of -1.72.

straight lean0 x2 thick: 7 bins of step 2.509, one layer each (k = 57 to 63). The excess fit is -5.00 against an error of -4.89. Bins 1 and 2 (k = 57, 58) have bone at j-1 that the cut removed (bins2_straight.txt). The canal line leans -7.13 degrees against a truth of -2.63.

straight x5 thin: excess fit -0.97, error -0.96, no cut binds. One bin (z +4.77) holds layers 153 and 154, and layer 154 is never read as its own row. straight x5 thick: excess fit -0.08, error -0.01.
suite18: straight thin error -0.11 (excess fit -0.13), thick +0.07 (excess fit -0.23). Each bin holds 5 to 12 layers. The x-strip dithers the staircase across columns, so the error is small.

Current reader over all 98 configs: max |error| 4.14 degrees thin (shapes lean0 x2) and 5.66 thick (shapes lean0 x2); median 0.40 thin and 0.39 thick. The 1.72 quoted for tilt 2 is the straight lean0 phantom only; pitched x2 thin is -3.02, straight lean+5 x2 thin -3.05.

Oracle (same bins, each least y moved back onto the true wall by its excess): max |error| 0.21 thin and 0.89 thick, median 0.01 and 0.03. |reader error - fit of the excess| has max 0.89 and median 0.02 over 98 configs.
No bins at all (least y of each lattice layer k, at that point's own z): max |error| 4.01 thin and 5.69 thick, the same as with bins. Removing the binning does not remove the error.
Bin phase shifted by 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 of a step: the spread of the reading is at most 1.05 degrees thin and 2.46 thick. The phase resamples a biased staircase; it is not the bias itself.

Bins half as wide (max(fz, 0.5)/2) miss the wall in some bins and give errors up to +12.31 (straight x2 thin) and +42.29 degrees (shapes lean+4 x2 thick). The current step is what keeps every bin on a wall voxel.

Cut removed (B plus the mask voxels up to 3 mm behind the cut line in the strip, same bins): straight x2 thin -1.72 -> +0.11; x2 thick -4.89 -> -1.42; pitched x2 thin -3.02 -> +0.12; straight lean+5 x2 thin -3.05 -> +0.05; shapes x2 thin -4.14 -> -1.30; shapes x2 thick -5.66 -> -2.19. Max |error| with the cut removed: 2.04 thin, 2.19 thick.
The cut binds in 10 thin and 10 thick configs, all at wall-to-lattice angles of 1 to 15 degrees, mostly x2. Configs with no cut: max |error| 2.04 thin (median 0.13) and 1.49 thick (median 0.24).
Pure staircase with no cut: straight lean+5 y12 thin errs +2.04 with 0 cut-bound bins, an oracle residual of -0.06 and a per-layer reading of +2.33.

Pure binning abscissa: straight lean+5 x5 thick (the wall lies on a lattice plane, relative angle 0.0, excess exactly 0.378 in every bin) errs +0.89. Using each point's own z gives -0.00, and the per-layer reading gives -0.00. The bin z offsets run -1.11, -1.21, +1.17, +1.06, +0.96, +0.86, +0.76 mm; layer 58 shares bin 2 with layer 57 and is never read. Max |reading with bin z - reading with the point's own z| is 0.89 thick and 0.17 thin.

Mask-free 2-D staircase model (staircase_model.txt: a plane wall on a lattice, least y per layer, 16.2 mm window, 144 lattice shifts). Thin: relative angle 2 degrees gives a median |error| of 2.00 and a max of 2.31 (period 22.9 mm); 5 degrees, median 0.68 and max 1.07; 10 degrees, max 0.88. Thick: 2 degrees, max 3.06; 5 degrees, max 2.30. The phantom's uncut errors lie inside this envelope.

The canal line's slab anterior edges against the true wall (canal.txt), straight x2 thin: excess +0.08 rising to +0.39 over z -4.0 to +5.3, then -0.37 at z +6.3 (one row step). The canal line errs -2.51 degrees there, the posterior wall reader -1.72. Across the cache the canal line's max |error| is 3.74 thin and 7.72 thick.
diagnose.implications_for_fix:
Re-binning will not fix this reader. Dropping the bins entirely (least y per lattice layer) still errs by up to 4.01 degrees on thin slices and 5.69 on thick. Narrower bins are worse: at half width some bins miss the wall voxel and the error reaches +12 to +42 degrees. Any change must keep every row on a wall voxel, either the current step or grouping by the scan's own k.

Three separate repairs, measured on these phantoms only:

(a) Abscissa. Fit each least y at its own point's z, not the bin centre. This removes the bin term: up to 0.89 degrees on thick slices, 0.17 on thin.

(b) The cut. Read the wall from the mask's own posterior surface in the midline strip, not from B as cut by the canal line. For example, take the mask's voxels a few mm behind the cut line, where only body wall lies at the midline, or move the cut behind the wall by a margin before taking least y. Removing the cut lowered the max error from 4.14 to 2.04 (thin) and from 5.66 to 2.19 (thick), and straight x2 thin from -1.72 to +0.11. Any change to the cut also changes everything else that uses B. anatomy.wall_slope's canal line, which sets the cut, has the same staircase (up to 7.72 degrees) and needs the same kind of repair.

(c) The staircase. After (a) and (b), up to about 2 degrees remains. It is the lattice staircase over a window shorter than its period, and the mask-free model says any least-y-per-layer line fit has it (median 2.00 degrees at a 2-degree relative angle). A fix needs information below one voxel, not a different bin. Options: a reading that uses where the row steps fall, such as a bone-versus-air parting on the lattice's own centres with its feasible slope range, in the manner of pedicle.parting and slope_range; fitting across many columns, where the strip dithers the steps, as it does at suite18; or the full height rather than its middle 60 percent. I did not build or score any of these candidates.

Not measured here: the downstream sagittal, end-plate and spinous errors of any variant (score.py does that); a per-slab decomposition of anatomy.wall_slope beyond the four configs in canal.txt; and any real mask.

diagnose.mechanism:
Two separate things go wrong, and the information limit tells them apart.

(1) The lattice itself does leave the slope free. Over posterior_wall_slope's region (3 mm either side of the midline, the middle 60 percent of the height, a span of about 15 to 16 mm), the bone centres can be parted from the canal's air centres by a whole range of surfaces. That range is wide whenever the wall runs nearly parallel to some family of lattice planes and crosses fewer than about one of them over the span. The wall then sits inside one strip of that family's spacing d, and its slope is free over roughly 2 atan(d / span). Three examples: on the aligned grid at lean 0 the strip is the 0.8 mm j-planes and the range is 6.5 degrees; on x2 the j-planes lie 2 degrees off and are crossed 0.71 times; on x10 thick at lean 0 the planes (0,2,1) are 0.424 mm apart and lie 0.24 degrees off, giving 3.83 degrees measured against a predicted 3.00. On 2.5 mm slices only about 6 layers fall in the span, so the range also depends on where those layers land.

To part the bone from the air at all, the surface needs an x^2 term (and an x term for the frame's roll). The phantom's wall curves forward by up to 0.16 mm at x = 3 mm, which is more than a thin lattice's phase steps. A line or plane in (y, z) parts nothing on 40 of 49 thin configs.

(2) The current reader sits well short of that limit, for two reasons that add up.

(a) The body cut. B is the bone in front of the canal's wall line (anatomy.body_in_front via wall_slope, wall_y0). Where that line's slope is wrong, it runs in front of the true wall at one end of the body and cuts posterior-wall bone out of B. In 49 of 98 configs it removes 1 to 32 bone centres inside the reader's band. The reader's per-bin minimum then follows the cut instead of the wall, and in 22 of those 49 the reader returns the canal line's own slope to within 0.3 degrees. anatomy.wall_slope has the same mechanism as posterior_wall_slope: each slab's anterior wall is the most posterior bone point in the slab, snapped to the lattice, and a Theil-Sen line through those points does not remove a bias that is systematic. It also feeds the cut, so its error passes into B.

(b) Per-bin extremes fitted by least squares. Each bin's most posterior bone centre lies between 0 and one row spacing in front of the wall, and that distance follows the lattice phase as a sawtooth in z. A line fitted to a sawtooth covering a fraction of a period, or a non-whole number of periods, is biased. It ignores the air centres that bound the wall from behind.
evidence: Method: scipy linprog (HiGHS) on the scan's own voxel centres in the vertebra's frame: |x - xc| <= 3 mm, the middle 60% of the midline body's height, within 4 mm of a rough wall line. Bone means v.is_bone (the L3 label); air means every centre the label does not hold. Across all 98 configs the label inside that band matches the phantom's own body test exactly (0 centres differ), so the air there is canal only. A surface parts the centres if bone lies on or in front of it and air on or behind it, with a margin of more than 1e-6 mm. All 98 configs were run.

Truth inside the range: for the curved family y = a + b z + c x + d x^2, 98 of 98 configs part and the frame-relative truth lies inside the range in all 98. The plane y = a + b z + c x parts 9 of 49 thin and 41 of 49 thick configs and holds the truth in 89 of 98. The line y = a + b z parts 9 of 49 thin and 37 of 49 thick and holds the truth in 77 of 98. Where they part nothing, the line and plane miss by at most 0.058 mm. Air centres sit up to 0.162 mm in front of the true plane, which is the wall's curve across x.

The least worst-case error any reader of this region can promise is half the range width: up to 3.27 degrees on thin slices (median 0.25) and up to 3.94 on thick (median 1.64). The far end of the range lies up to 4.00 (thin aligned), 3.00 (thin x2), 5.00 (thick aligned) and 7.00 (thick x2) degrees from the truth.

Where the widest-margin surface falls in the range (median position from 0 to 1): about 0.5 on aligned, x5, x10 and t25; 0.11 on thin x2 and 0.20 on thick x2; 0.68 on thin suite18. diagnose.mechanism:
anatomy's canal line (anatomy.wall_slope) goes wrong for the same reason body.posterior_wall_slope does, and the second inherits the first's error.

Both readers do the same thing. Along the frame's z they take, in each slab or bin, the outermost voxel centre of bone beside the wall and fit a line through those points.
- body.posterior_wall_slope takes the least y in a 3 mm strip, per bin of max(fz, 0.5) mm, over the middle 60 per cent of the height, and fits by least squares.
- The canal line takes each full ring's anterior wall from scanimport.geometry.canal_walls: the least y of bone within 0.75 pixel of the hole's middle, moved back half a gap by G.surface. It fits these by Theil-Sen, using pairs at least 4 mm apart.

For a plane wall, the first lattice centre inside it lies between 0 and one row step beyond the wall. That excess climbs or falls at tan(angle between the wall and the nearest lattice column). It jumps back by one row step every row step / tan(angle) mm, so the extremes trace a staircase.
- If the window holds no jump, the line follows the lattice column instead of the wall.
- If the window holds one jump, the jump sets the slope, by roughly atan(1.5 x step / window) under least squares.
- On an aligned grid this only happens where the wall leans against the lattice. A wall lying along the lattice reads exactly.

The canal line has two further weaknesses:
- A shorter window: the rings span 7.5 to 13.8 mm on the straight and pitched phantoms, and only 4 to 6 rings on 2.5 mm slices, with as few as 3 pairs.
- A second error source, the per-slab half-gap from edge_gap, which on tilted grids flips between its layer and cluster cases from slab to slab.

The two readers are also coupled. body.posterior_wall_slope reads B = v.body_pts, the body that anatomy.body_in_front cut along the canal line. That line is extrapolated over the whole body height, past the rings. Where the line leans off the wall, the cut passes in front of the wall's outermost centres in some bins, and the posterior reader then reads the cut. So the canal line's error leaks into the pedicle's sagittal angle, both end-plate inclinations and the spinous angle.

The README's "the canal walls lean half as far" is this staircase, not a halving. On the joint phantom, in the column's-line frame, the scanner's slice axis lay at -4.15 degrees, about half-way to the wall's -7.99. The rings' 9 mm span held no jump, so the line read the slice axis.

candidates.name: Candidate A, lattice-native wall reader (per-line edges, least-squares quadric, clamped to the lattice's free range)
candidates.summary:
How it reads the wall. It reads the vertebra's own label (v.idx, v.is_bone), not the body B that the canal line cut, so the cut no longer decides any edge. B is used only for the wall's height at the midline, which sets the middle-60-percent window as the current reader does.

It walks the scan axis that runs most nearly along the frame's y. Each lattice line along that axis is one row of one layer, and it gives one edge: the midpoint between the last centre of a solid run of bone and the first air centre behind it, placed at that midpoint's own (x, y, z) in the frame. So no layer is missed or caught twice, and there are no z bins. The edges come from a band of half-width min(6 mm, a quarter of the canal's width at its full rings), about 5.6 to 6.0 mm on these phantoms. That gives 200 to 270 edges on thin slices and 72 to 99 on thick ones.

It fits the surface y = a + b z + c x + d x^2 to the edges by least squares (x measured from xc). The x terms take up the frame's roll and the wall's curve across the midline, which is what makes the wider band usable. It drops edges more than one lattice step off the surface and fits again; none were dropped on clean phantoms. It returns b.

The least-squares fit still follows the half-step staircase where the window holds few row steps. I checked this with diag.py: fitting the phantom's true crossing points on the same lines gives the truth exactly (suite18 thick +0.01 against +0.01; x2 thin -0.07 against -0.07). So all the remaining error is the lattice's quantisation, not the model or the frame.

The clamp. Two linear programs, like pedicle.slope_range, give the least and greatest b of any surface in the same family that keeps each edge's bone centre in front and its air centre behind, with 1e-6 mm of room. The truth lay inside this range in every config where it was found (48 of 48 thin, 49 of 49 thick). Where the least-squares b falls outside the range, it is moved to the nearer end. That happened in 19 thin and 8 thick configs, and it is the main gain: without the clamp the max error is 1.18 thin and 1.13 thick; with it, 0.30 and 0.79. Where no surface parts the centres, the least-squares b stands.

Bounds I set, from the geometry:
- the band, as above;
- edges only within a quarter of the canal's median depth (about 3.75 mm) of the canal's line, in front or behind. The canal line errs by up to 7.7 degrees, about 1.1 mm at the window's ends, so this keeps out the lamina, the spinous process and lines that leave the body through an end-plate;
- a solid run of at least 3 mm of bone in front of each edge;
- refusal where there are no full rings, fewer than 8 edges, or edges spanning less than half the window.

I changed two of these after seeing failures, and neither changed the clean cache score. The gate replaced 'in front of the canal's middle' after ragged thick labels let end-plate exits in (errors up to 17 degrees). The 1e-6 mm room was added after the 80-percent-height variant collapsed the range to one wrong slope.

The information-limit question: my reader reads every config and refuses none on freedom grounds. It reports the range (free_lo_deg, free_hi_deg, free_deg) in info so a caller can refuse.
- Range widths: thin median 0.26 and max 2.18 degrees; thick median 1.03 and max 7.87.
- The 7.87 is straight_lean+5_x5_thick. The wall lies on a lattice plane there, so the least-squares fit is exact (error 0.00) although the lattice leaves 7.9 degrees free.
- The other wide thick configs (2.98 to 3.28 degrees) read within 0.51.
- The error is within half the range's width in 36 of 49 thin and 40 of 49 thick configs.

Other measurements:
- Downstream, thin: pedicle sagittal max 2.02 (current 3.42; with the true wall 1.83); end-plate inclinations 1.38 and 1.59 (true wall 1.34 and 1.53); spinous 1.80 (true wall 1.87).
- Downstream, thick: 2.79, 3.80 and 5.83, against 2.53, 4.06 and 5.67 with the true wall. What remains there is the rim and spinous readings' own error, not the wall's.
- Held out, 16 phantoms not in the cache (the test suite's ThickSlices and Overhang, tilts 3 and 7 degrees, two other lattice phases at x2 and aligned): max 0.64 thin (current 2.18) and 1.24 thick (current 4.51). ThickSlices reads -0.02 against the current -4.51, and its endplate_incl error drops from +4.55 to +0.06.
- The phantom tests (Straight, Shapes, PitchedDown, Overhang, ThickSlices, LateralMass) pass 19 of 19 with the reader swapped in-process, as they do with the current one.
- About 8 to 10 ms per vertebra, against 0.7 ms now.

It takes a per-slab extreme of the canal's anterior wall, which has the same staircase, and Theil-Sen does not remove a systematic bias. My reader now uses it only as the gate above. candidates.name: Candidate B: posterior wall parted from the canal by a linear program (widest margin, least-crossing fallback, slope range)
candidates.summary:
How it reads the wall. slope(v, B, xc) takes the scan's own voxel centres in the vertebra's frame over the same region posterior_wall_slope reads: within 3 mm of xc, over the middle 60 percent of the midline body's height. Front to back it keeps the centres within half the canal's median midline depth (full rings' ap / 2, about 8 mm on the phantoms) of the canal's wall line, the line the body was cut at. "Bone" is the vertebra's own label (v.is_bone), not B, so the cut can no longer remove wall voxels. B only sets the height window. "Not body" is every centre the label does not hold in that box. At the midline, within half the canal's depth of the wall, that is the canal: the lamina and spinous process lie behind the canal's middle, the same margin column.wall_corner uses. On all 98 configs the box held only wall bone and canal; nothing crossed.

The program. It finds the surface y = a + b z' + c x' + d x'^2 that parts bone (in front) from canal (behind) with the widest margin, using scipy linprog (HiGHS). z' is measured from the window's middle and x' from xc. The c term absorbs the frame's roll, the d term the wall's curve across the strip. The widest margin is often reached by a range of b, so the reading is the middle of that range. Two more programs give the range of b over every surface that still parts the centres (pedicle.slope_range's rule); info carries it as lo_deg, hi_deg and width_deg. Info also carries margin_mm, n_bone, n_canal, near, across and worst_mm.

Fallback and refusal. Where the widest margin is not positive, a least-crossing program (sum of crossings, sparse matrix) marks the centres across. Those are set aside and the rest are parted by the widest margin. The reading is refused (NAN plus "why") in five cases:
- no full canal ring;
- fewer than 20 centres of bone or of canal;
- more than 10 percent of the centres within 2 rows of the surface lie across;
- one centre lies more than 1.5 rows (1.5 * v.fy) across;
- the slope range is wider than 9 degrees.

The bounds I set, and why:
- The three main bounds are pedicle.py's own for its surfaces: VIOLATED_SHARE 0.1, SURFACE_LAYERS 1.5 (as rows) and FREEDOM_DEG 9. One rule for "the lattice leaves this angle too free" or "this is not one surface" across the module.
- The crossing bound has a geometric reason. A smooth wall cut by the lattice at any phase is bracketed within one row, so a deeper crossing is a notch, a lip or a fragment.
- MIN_EACH 20, NEAR_ROWS 2 and the 10 mm margin cap only keep the programs bounded. None is set from the cache's truths.

Scored on the full cache (98 pickles). Every config parts: least margin 0.004 mm thin and 0.014 mm thick, nothing across. The truth lies inside the reported slope range in 98 of 98. Nothing is refused, so on the phantoms the fallback and the refusals never fire. The numbers equal the limit lens's x3_h60 widest-margin reader:
- Wall error, thin: max 1.00, median 0.05 (current reader 4.14, 0.40).
- Wall error, thick: max 2.32, median 0.24 (current 5.66, 0.39).
- Thin downstream maxima against the current reader's: sagittal 1.95 vs 3.42, endplate_incl 1.41 vs 3.56, endplate_lower_incl 2.44 vs 5.61, spinous 2.64 vs 3.31.
- Thick downstream maxima: endplate_incl 3.94 vs 6.97, endplate_lower 3.93 vs 6.96, spinous 5.58 vs 7.52. These include the raw readings' own errors. The cache reads no thick-slice sagittal angle.
- It is worse than the current reader on two thick grids: suite18 (1.42 vs 0.77) and y12 (1.24 vs 0.61).

Configs the limit lens says cannot be pinned (wide ranges): they are read, not refused. The widest range on the cache is 7.87 degrees (thin median 0.51, max 6.54; thick median 3.28, max 7.87), all under the 9 degree bound.
- Where the lattice gives no crossing in the window, the widest-margin surface follows the lattice planes. Example: the x2 thick lean-0 phantoms read the lattice and err 1.9 to 2.3 inside a 4.92 degree range.
- On aligned thin grids the range is 5.4 to 6.5 degrees, but the reading is exact to 0.08 by symmetry.
- The reading's error was at most 0.60 of the range's width in all 98 configs, and at most half the width in 97. So width_deg / 2 works as a rough error bar.
- A stricter bound mostly refuses good readings. At 4 degrees it would refuse 7 thin and 16 thick configs; at 6 degrees the 4 thin refusals are the aligned ones that err 0.00.

Wider regions, measured but not adopted (choosing one by its error would be tuning to the truths):
- 3 mm and 80 percent of the height: max 1.00 thin and 1.54 thick, median 0.04 and 0.17.
- 6 mm and 80 percent: max 1.00 thin (shapes_lean+4_x5_thin, which reads the same lattice direction at every region) and 0.24 thick, median 0.01 and 0.07.

Time, measured with the vertebra already loaded: median 0.057 s per config on thin slices (max 0.091), 0.023 s on thick. The current reader takes 0.0014 and 0.0005 s.

The least-crossing path, tested only on phantoms altered by hand. I cut notches into the wall, put a speck in the canal, added a lip at the window's top, and bowed the wall 0.4 or 0.8 mm. That is 5 configs times 11 changes, 55 readings, of which 20 were refused.

- 1 mm central notches read within 0.8 degrees, or are refused.
- Structures at one end of the window pull the surface and often pass every bound. A 2 mm notch at the top read +5.00 and +11.76 unrefused. A lip 1 to 2 mm deep read -3.0 to -5.8 unrefused in 7 of 10. Bows moved the reading by up to 3.9 degrees (worst -5.84 against -1.92 unaltered).

candidates.name: C: boundary midpoints by least squares
candidates.summary:
How it reads the wall. First it picks the lattice axis whose direction in the frame lies closest to y, and steps along it toward the canal. Each scan line on that axis is a candidate if its midpoint lies within 3 mm of xc, falls in the middle 60 percent of the midline body's height (z0 and z1 taken from B's midline strip, as the current reader does), and sits within half the canal's depth (the median ap of the full rings, about 8 mm) of the canal's wall line. On each such line it takes the most posterior entry from not-bone into bone, using the vertebra's own label (v.is_bone over the scan's lattice). The cut body B gives only xc and the height. The wall point is the midpoint of the bone centre and the air centre behind it. A least-squares surface y = a + b z + c x + d x^2 is fitted through these points, and up to 3 trimming rounds drop points more than one whole step |d_y - b d_z| off the fit (at most 20 percent per round). It returns b. info carries the pair count, the rms residual over the step, and the range of slopes of every line that keeps each pair straddled once the fitted x terms are taken off.

Bounds I set, and why:
- The gate is half the canal's depth, the same margin column.wall_corner uses. A pair further back than that lies on the arch's side.
- The trim bound is one step. A midpoint of a pair that straddles a plane wall lies within half a step of it, and the fit lies within another half step.
- MIN_PAIRS = 12, the same as G.MIN_CHORD_POINTS, and MIN_LAYERS = 3, the current reader's minimum.
- The 3 mm band and the 60 percent window are inherited from the current reader.
- Nothing was set from the cache's truths.

- Reading the label instead of B. The same reader with B as inside gives 3.46 thin and 5.50 thick.
- The x terms make no difference: with no x terms the maxima are 1.63 and 2.02.
- Trimming never fires: 0 points dropped in 98 configs.
- Taking every entry on a line rather than only the most posterior one changes nothing.

- Sagittal angle: 2.37 / 3.42 / 1.83
- endplate_incl: 1.61 / 3.56 / 1.34
- endplate_lower_incl: 2.35 / 5.61 / 1.53

verdict.gate:
Refuse (return NAN with a reason; the four consumers then read NaN, never 0.0) where:
- no full canal ring exists;
- fewer than G.MIN_CHORD_POINTS (12) edges lie within one lattice step of the fitted surface;
- the edges span less than half the window's height;
- the lattice leaves the slope free over more than FREEDOM_DEG = 9 degrees, pedicle's own bound for its climb, kept so the module has one rule.

The freedom is the linear-program range where the label parts. Elsewhere it is the range a clean digitisation of the fitted surface would leave on the same scan lines. Where the label parts, the two agree: median difference 0.05 deg thin, 0.09 thick.

Cost of these refusals on the phantoms: none of the 98 clean configs. Among the 1,176 altered readings, 3, all thick: 1 lip and 2 edge cuts. At 9 degrees the freedom refuses 0 thin and 8 thick of 637 altered readings; those 8 erred at most 1.71.

Flag but keep the reading where free_deg > 3 degrees, so that its half-width passes the suite's 1.5-degree tolerance for the sagittal angle and the inclinations. That flags 0 thin and 3 thick clean configs; thick free_deg has median 1.03 and max 7.87. Also carry rms_over_step, edges, dropped and parted in the trace. rms_over_step is 0.28 on clean labels (a clean digitisation gives 1/sqrt(12) = 0.29) and 0.36 to 0.43 median on ragged or flipped labels: a weak sign of a ragged label, not a gate.

Why not refuse tighter: the freedom does not rank the errors. The rank correlation of |error| with freedom is 0.14 thin and 0.11 thick over the altered sets. A bound of 4 degrees would refuse 57 thin and 91 thick of 637 altered readings, whose median error, 0.25 and 0.39, is barely above that of the readings kept (0.12 and 0.27). B's author found the same: a 4-degree bound mostly refuses good readings.

What the freedom does promise: where the label parts, the clamped reading and the truth both lie in the range, so the width bounds the error. On clean configs |error| was at most the width in 47/49 thin and 48/49 thick, and at most half of it in 40/49 and 45/49.

Not gated: a proud structure inside the window on thick slices, and the lean of a ragged label. Neither is visible to any statistic I measured.
verdict.combine:
From B, adopt four things:
- the parting linear program with PART_MM room, as the clamp's range;
- pedicle.FREEDOM_DEG (9) as the refusal bound;
- returning NAN with a reason in place of the silent 0.0;
- its finding that the range's half-width is an honest error bar but a poor refusal criterion.

Leave B's widest-margin reading, its least-crossing fallback and its refusals on crossings out: on real-looking labels they refuse most readings.

From C, take nothing into the code. Its measured lesson stands: the label read in place of the cut body is what carries the gain, and the x terms barely matter at 3 mm. Its half-canal gate is the reason the 4 mm channel's floor gets in, so keep A's quarter-depth gate. Do not adopt C's riser variant (cand_crack.py): its weights are chosen, and its own author found it fragile under jitter.

My own grafts onto A, all measured:
- Least trimmed squares as the start: keep 75 percent, deterministic starts from the whole set and the window's lower, middle and upper halves. Random starts changed nothing (judge/det_table.txt).
- A Tukey biweight polish with scale two lattice steps along y.
- The edge set for the programs and the span check taken again from the final fit, not from the first fit.
- The clean-digitisation range, so a freedom exists on ragged masks.

On anatomy.wall_slope (the canal line): it shares the mechanism. Its per-slab extremes trace the same staircase, and Theil-Sen does not remove a systematic bias; it errs up to 3.74 thin and 7.72 thick on the cache. The new reader uses it only as a gate of about 4 mm, so its error no longer reaches the wall reading. Repair it separately with the same lattice reading, because it also sets the body cut, Panjabi's depths, canal_ap_lateral_film and morphoview's lines.

1. morphometry/body.py: add posterior_wall(v, B, xc) -> (slope, info). posterior_wall_slope(v, B, xc) returns its slope, NAN on refusal (today it returns 0.0 silently). Steps:
   (a) Take the full rings. Band half-width = min(6 mm, 0.25 x the rings' median width). Gate reach = 0.25 x the rings' median ap.
   (b) Window: the middle 60 percent of the z extent of B within the band of xc. B gives only this window and xc.
   (c) Walk the scan axis most nearly along the frame's y, stepping posteriorly. Edge candidates are the vertebra's voxels (v.idx, v.loc) that meet three tests:
       - within the gate of the canal line (|square_to_wall(v, loc)[:,1] - v.wall_y0| <= reach);
       - air one step behind (not v.is_bone);
       - bone for every step over RUN_MM = 3 mm in front.
       Each edge is the midpoint of that bone centre and the air centre. Keep the most posterior edge on each scan line, inside the band and window.

   (e) good = |residual| <= |step_y|. Refuse below 12 good edges, or a good span under half the window.
   (f) Run two linprog programs (HiGHS) for the least and greatest b of the family that keeps each good bone centre in front and its air centre behind by more than PART_MM = 1e-6. If they part, clamp b into that range. If not, run the same programs on the centres either side of where the fitted surface crosses each edge's scan line (proposed.clean_digitisation) for the range alone.
